reading.body:
LinkedIn reported $237.6 million in securities sold across five Form D filings from 2010 to 2014, with the largest single offering at $119.6 million in 2014.

The filings cluster in 2011, 2013, and 2014, and the reported amounts rise from $21.2 million to $119.6 million. That pattern suggests growing capital needs as the company scaled, but Form D covers only exempt offerings, not total funding or operating costs. The 2010 filing lists a first sale in 2007, so the reported amounts span a longer period than the filing dates alone indicate.

LinkedIn holds 260 granted patents, including recent titles on regularized model adaptation for recommendations and distributed graph database writes. These are relevant to serving machine learning features at scale, but the data contains no figures on data centers, energy use, GPUs, or grid connections. It therefore cannot support any claim about compute or power constraints for this company.

profile_text.body:
LinkedIn describes itself as a professional network with 1 billion members. Its site states that it lets users manage their professional identity, build and engage with a professional network, and access knowledge, insights, and opportunities. The site lists job categories such as engineering, business development, finance, and administrative roles, and software categories including CRM software, human resources management systems, recruiting software, sales intelligence software, and social networking software.

LinkedIn was founded in 2003 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, United States. It is a for-profit company. It has 281 legal exposure entries in California, with no individual cases listed. In AI-related offerings, LinkedIn has an MCP integration named ai.com.mcp/linkedin, described as LinkedIn API as MCP tools to retrieve profile data and publish content, powered by HAPI MCP.
